{"message":"I really appreciate your patience. Your data and roaming are working, your APN has the MMSC set, and we added APN type mms. At this point, the most likely blockers are phone-side settings specific to MMS while roaming. I’ll give very simple steps for two things: (1) how to find your phone’s model/version and (2) a short set of targeted fixes that often resolve MMS-on-roaming.

A) Easiest way to find your phone’s Model and Android version
- Open the Settings app (gray gear icon).
- At the very top of Settings, tap the search bar and type: About
- Tap the result that says About phone (or About device).
- On that screen, look for:
  • Model (or Model name)
  • Android version (if you see “Software information,” tap it to reveal Android version)
Please tell me exactly what it says for both.

B) Targeted MMS fixes (please do these in order, then test)
Why: These address common MMS blockers while roaming—messaging app defaults, RCS interference, background data for the app, APN protocol, and 5G roaming quirks.

1) Make sure your messaging app is the Default SMS app
- Settings > Apps > Default apps > SMS app > select “Messages” (or your main texting app).

2) Turn OFF Chat features (RCS) in the Messages app
- Open the Messages app.
- Tap your profile picture or the three dots (top right) > Settings.
- Tap Chat features (or RCS chats) > turn Off.

3) Enable MMS auto‑download (including when roaming)
- In Messages app: Settings > Advanced (or More settings).
- Turn ON Auto-download MMS (and if you see “Auto-download MMS when roaming,” turn that ON too).

4) Allow background/unrestricted data for the Messages app
- Settings > Apps > Messages > Mobile data & Wi‑Fi (or Data usage).
- Turn ON Background data.
- Turn ON Unrestricted data usage (or “Allow data usage while Data Saver is on”).

5) Clear cache for the Messages app (safe; does not delete messages/photos)
- Settings > Apps > Messages > Storage & cache > Clear cache. Do NOT tap Clear storage.

6) Adjust APN protocol for roaming MMS
- Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Mobile network (SIMs) > Access Point Names.
- Tap your selected APN (the one we created).
- Find APN protocol and APN roaming protocol (scroll down; some phones hide these under “Advanced”).
- Set both to IPv4 (if there’s a choice like IPv4/IPv6, pick IPv4 first; we can try IPv4/IPv6 later).
- Menu (•••) > Save.
- Restart the phone.

7) Temporarily set network to 4G only
- Settings > Mobile network (or SIMs) > Preferred network type.
- Choose LTE/4G only (not 5G) for this test.

8) Ensure date & time are automatic
- Settings > System > Date & time.
- Turn ON “Use network-provided time” and “Use network-provided time zone.”

9) Test with a small image
- Keep Wi‑Fi OFF.
- Load example.com (confirm data is fast).
- Send a small picture (e.g., a screenshot or a photo under ~500 KB) to:
  • Your own number, and
  • A different contact.
- Also ask a friend to send a picture message to you (to see if receiving works).

Please tell me:
- Your phone’s Model and Android version (from step A).
- Which of the above steps you completed.
- Whether sending to another contact worked, and if you could receive an MMS from someone else.

If it still fails after these, the next step is to have a human specialist check your MMS provisioning while roaming on our side. I can transfer you right away after your update, or sooner if you prefer. Your photos are safe during all of this—none of these steps delete photos."}

{"message":"Thanks for the quick update. Since roaming is now enabled on your line (I did that on our side) and your phone’s Airplane Mode/Data/Roaming are set correctly, the next step is to help your phone register on a local network in France. Here’s my plan and why, plus what to do right now.

Why these steps
- Your phone needs to “handshake” with a partner network abroad. A quick radio refresh and, if needed, a reboot usually resolves no‑signal after changing settings.
- Once we get any signal (bars + 4G/LTE/5G), we’ll add the 2 GB you requested so MMS can use data right away.

Do this now (stop as soon as you get signal and tell me what you see):
1) Fast network refresh
   - Turn Airplane Mode ON for 20 seconds, then turn it OFF again.
   - Wait up to 2 minutes. Watch for signal bars and a 4G/LTE/5G indicator.
2) If still no signal after 2 minutes
   - Reboot your phone (full restart), then wait another 2 minutes after it powers back on for network registration.
3) If still no signal after the reboot
   - Check network mode:
     • iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Voice & Data: set to 5G On/Auto (or LTE).
     • Android: Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Mobile network > Preferred network type: set to 4G/5G preferred.
   - Give it another 2 minutes.
4) If still no signal
   - Check if the phone shows any SIM error (e.g., “No SIM” or “SIM locked”). If it does, tell me exactly what it says. If there’s no error, power off, remove and reinsert the SIM, then power on and wait 2 minutes.

What I’ll do about the data refuel
- You asked for 2 GB at $4. I can apply it immediately or wait until you see signal—your choice. It will post to your line either way, but MMS can’t send until the phone has signal.

Please reply with:
- The result after Step 1 (did any bars or 4G/LTE/5G appear?). If not, proceed to Step 2 and tell me what you see after the reboot.
- Whether you want me to add the 2 GB now or wait until signal appears."}

Please do these in order (keep Wi‑Fi OFF during testing) and tell me the results:

1) Quick data check
- Try loading example.com in your browser OR run a quick speed test. Let me know if the page loads or the speed test result (unknown/very poor/poor/fair/good/excellent).

2) Wi‑Fi Calling
- iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Wi‑Fi Calling > set OFF.
- Android: Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Mobile network > Wi‑Fi Calling > set OFF.
- Reason: Some carriers don’t support MMS over Wi‑Fi Calling while roaming.

- Data Saver: If enabled, turn it OFF.
  • iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Low Data Mode OFF.
  • Android: Settings > Network & Internet > Data Saver > OFF.
- VPN: If a VPN is connected, disconnect it.
  • iPhone: Settings > VPN > toggle OFF.
  • Android: Settings > Network & Internet > VPN > Disconnect.

- Roaming setting on the line if you’re traveling

}

messages.content:
{
  "message": "Great question. Yes—the little airplane icon means Airplane Mode is ON, which turns off all wireless connections. That will stop MMS from working. It’s safe to turn it OFF; it won’t delete anything on your phone (photos, messages, apps).

Let’s do this step by step. Please follow the set that matches your phone’s menus. If something doesn’t match, stop and tell me what you see, and I’ll adjust.

Step 1: Turn OFF Airplane Mode
- iPhone:
  1) Open Control Center (swipe down from the top-right corner on newer iPhones; swipe up from the bottom on older models).
  2) Tap the airplane icon so it is NOT lit/colored (it should turn gray).
  Or: Settings > Airplane Mode > turn it OFF.
  3) Wait ~10–20 seconds for signal bars and 4G/LTE/5G to appear.

- Android:
  1) Swipe down from the top to open Quick Settings.
  2) Tap the Airplane Mode tile so it turns OFF.
  Or: Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Airplane mode > OFF.
  3) Wait ~10–20 seconds for signal bars and 4G/LTE/5G to appear.

Once the airplane icon disappears and you see signal bars:

Step 2: Make sure Mobile Data is ON
- iPhone: Settings > Cellular (or Mobile Data) > turn “Cellular Data” ON.
- Android: Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Mobile network (or SIMs) > turn “Mobile data” ON.

Step 3: Turn Data Roaming ON (you’re in France)
- iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > turn “Data Roaming” ON.
- Android: Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Mobile network (or SIMs) > turn “Data roaming” ON.

Step 4: Turn Wi‑Fi OFF temporarily (just for the test), and Wi‑Fi Calling OFF
- iPhone: Control Center > tap Wi‑Fi to OFF; then Settings > Cellular > Wi‑Fi Calling > OFF.
- Android: Quick Settings > Wi‑Fi OFF; then Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Wi‑Fi Calling > OFF.

Step 5: Test
- Open your web browser and load any webpage (to confirm mobile data works).
- Then try sending a picture message (MMS).

Why these steps: Airplane Mode blocks all connections; turning it OFF restores service. MMS needs working mobile data, and because you’re abroad, Data Roaming must be ON on the phone. Turning Wi‑Fi/Wi‑Fi Calling off briefly ensures the test uses mobile data.

Please do Step 1 first and tell me: did the airplane icon disappear, and do you now see signal bars with 4G/LTE/5G? Once that’s confirmed, we’ll proceed with Steps 2–5 together. And don’t worry—toggling these settings won’t erase any of your content."
}

   - Insert a SIM eject tool or a small straightened paperclip into the tiny hole; press gently until the tray pops out.

1) Restart the phone (power OFF, then ON) and wait 60 seconds after boot.
2) Check if the message still says SIM missing.
3) If it still says SIM missing after a restart, we may need to re-provision your eSIM on our side. I can help with that next.

Why these steps: “SIM missing” is usually a physical contact issue (fixed by reseating). If there’s no tray, an eSIM glitch can be cleared by a restart; otherwise we’ll re-provision the eSIM. And rest assured: none of these steps will delete any of your photos or personal data."
}

If MMS still won’t send, the most common remaining causes are: Wi‑Fi/Wi‑Fi Calling interference, a VPN, Data Saver/Low Data Mode, or the phone’s MMS server settings (APN/MMSC) needing a reset. None of the steps below will delete your photos or personal data.

Let’s try these in order. If a menu name doesn’t match what you see, stop and tell me what you see.

Step 1: Make sure MMS uses mobile data (quick test)
- Turn Wi‑Fi OFF temporarily.
- Turn Wi‑Fi Calling OFF.
- Confirm you can load a webpage using mobile data only.
Then try sending a picture message again.

iPhone:
- Wi‑Fi OFF: Control Center > tap Wi‑Fi so it’s OFF.
- Wi‑Fi Calling OFF: Settings > Cellular > Wi‑Fi Calling > OFF.
- Also check Messages setting: Settings > Messages > make sure “MMS Messaging” is ON.

Android:
- Wi‑Fi OFF: Swipe down > tap Wi‑Fi tile OFF.
- Wi‑Fi Calling OFF: Settings > Network & internet (or Connections) > Wi‑Fi Calling > OFF.
- Also check Messages permissions: Settings > Apps > Messages > Permissions > allow SMS and Photos/Media/Storage.

If it still won’t send, continue.

Step 2: Make sure no VPN or Data Saver is interfering
- Turn OFF any VPN (if you use one).
- Turn OFF Data Saver/Low Data Mode.

iPhone:
- VPN: Settings > VPN > turn OFF.
- Low Data Mode: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Data Mode > pick Standard (not Low Data Mode).

Android:
- VPN: Settings > Network & internet > VPN > Disconnect.
- Data Saver: Settings > Network & internet > Data Saver > OFF.

If it still won’t send, continue.

Step 3: Reset the APN/MMS settings, then reboot (most reliable fix)
This restores the MMSC server settings MMS needs. After resetting, restart the phone.

Android (APN reset):
- Settings > Network & internet (or Connections) > Mobile network (or SIMs) > Access Point Names.
- Tap the menu (⋮) > Reset to default (or “Restore default settings”).
- Then restart the phone (power off, wait 10 seconds, power on).

iPhone (network settings reset resets MMS/APN):
- Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings.
- Your saved Wi‑Fi networks and VPN settings will be removed, but photos and personal data remain untouched.
- After the reset, the phone restarts automatically.

After the reboot
- Keep Wi‑Fi OFF for the test, ensure Mobile/Cellular Data ON and Data Roaming ON (you’re in France).
- Wait 30–60 seconds on the home screen.
- Open a webpage to confirm mobile data works, then try sending a picture message.

If it still won’t send after these steps, tell me exactly what you see (for example: “still spinning,” any error text, or if the Messages/Messaging app shows a specific warning). Also let me know whether your menus looked more like iPhone or Android as you went, and I’ll tailor the next step precisely."
}
